vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-cws-publisher
Version: 0.1.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate workflow for automating the packaging and publishing of Chrome extensions. It includes scripts for generating marketing assets using headless Chrome, scanning for potential secret leaks (scan_publish_surface.py), and driving Chrome Web Store submissions via OpenClaw browser automation (publish_extension.py). The code is well-structured, lacks obfuscation, and its behavior aligns strictly with the stated purpose of streamlining extension releases.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and scripts align with its stated purpose (packaging, scanning, asset generation, and automated Chrome Web Store submission via OpenClaw); nothing requests unrelated credentials or installs arbitrary remote code.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the included scripts: inventorying manifests, building ZIPs, rendering assets, scanning for leak-like patterns, generating metadata, and driving OpenClaw browser automation. The declared required binaries (openclaw, clawhub, gh, git, sips, python3) are proportionate to these tasks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts perform broad filesystem reads under the user-provided search-root (inventory and leak scans), render pages via a local Chrome binary, and use OpenClaw to snapshot and automate the Web Store dashboard. This is coherent for the publishing use case, but the scan/inventory steps will read any files under the supplied search-root (so avoid pointing it at your whole home or system directories). OpenClaw snapshots and uploads are saved locally, but the automation tooling (openclaw) may itself interact with network endpoints depending on that tool's behavior — the skill's code does not independently send data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction/code-only and runs local Python scripts. There are no downloads, archive extraction, or remote install URLs in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or secrets. It expects certain CLIs to be available; those CLIs (gh, clawhub, openclaw) may themselves require auth tokens in the environment or configured credentials to operate, but the skill does not request unrelated credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. It writes artifacts into the project dist/docs directories and temporary Chrome profile dirs only.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says, but take these precautions before running it: 1) Supply a narrow search-root (e.g., the extension repo) rather than your entire home directory to avoid scanning unrelated files. 2) Review snapshots saved under dist/openclaw before publishing — the automation captures dashboard HTML/text which may contain sensitive info. 3) Understand that OpenClaw, gh, and clawhub CLIs may use their own credentials/config (if present) to act; only run the publish step when you intend to use those accounts. 4) The marketing asset renderer uses macOS-only tools (sips) and expects Chrome at macOS paths; run that step only on a compatible machine or adjust the script. 5) If you are unsure, run the non-publish steps (asset generation, scan, build) first and inspect outputs before invoking automated submission.
